task_description: The team must count how many High Energy Physics - Lattice (hep-lat) articles listed on arXiv for January 2020 had a PostScript (.ps) version available. On arXiv's listing/format pages each paper exposes download formats, and a subset of older-style TeX submissions offer an 'Author supplied PostScript' (ps) link in addition to PDF. The gold answer is 31 — meaning 31 of the January-2020 hep-lat entries actually had a ps option when their per-article format pages are checked.
final_vs_expected: produced 0 vs gold 31 — the team concluded zero papers had ps because the listing page only shows [pdf, other] and the two sampled format pages happened to lack ps, never checking per-article format pages systematically (where ps appears for TeX submissions).
primary_cause: Single-agent methodological/capability error: WebResearcher inferred ps-availability from the listing's '[pdf, other]' bracket and a 2-paper sample instead of querying each article's /format page, where ps actually appears, so the true count (31) was never found.
mast_rationale: 1.1 (disobey task spec): the task demands a count of articles WITH ps; the team answered the inverse-looking 0 by checking the wrong surface (the listing bracket) rather than per-paper format pages that the task implicitly requires. 3.2 (no/incomplete verification): no agent ever performed the systematic per-entry check; the listing's '[pdf, other]' bracket does not encode ps availability, so the absence of a ps token there is not evidence. 3.3 (incorrect verification / verification theater): Critic repeatedly and correctly flagged that 0 was unproven (turns 2,4,6), yet the Finalizer at turn 8 emitted 'FINAL ANSWER: 0' anyway, accepting an unverified wrong number. 2.6 (reasoning-action mismatch): WebResearcher's own reasoning admitted it 'can't fully verify all 97 due to truncation' and that 0 was unproven, yet it had earlier published '0' and the team finalized on it.
trace_narrative: Turn 1: WebResearcher searches arXiv, fetches the Jan-2020 hep-lat list (97 entries: 54 hep-lat + 43 cross-lists), and inspects two format pages (2001.00032, 2001.04398). It privately notes 'arXiv has disabled ps for newer submissions' and that the list shows only [pdf, other], then publishes that 0 articles had ps, citing the list, the year-stats page, and one format page. Turn 2: Critic correctly objects — 0 is 'not actually proven', only 'examples' were checked, the format page is 'a general policy page', and demands either a systematic per-entry check or a source reporting the count. Turn 3: WebResearcher does keyword/site searches for 'ps' in the listing, finds nothing, and publishes that it 'couldn't verify a definitive count' and lacks proof of exactly 0. Turn 4: Critic reiterates that 0 is unproven for all 97 entries and only two papers were format-checked. Turn 5: WebResearcher fetches the full list (show=2000), still sees only [pdf, other], and now reverses to publish that 'the evidence now supports 0'. Turn 6: Critic again says the page contents weren't shown and no item-by-item audit exists; asks for an audit of all 97. Turn 7: WebResearcher honestly retreats: 'I can't honestly prove a definitive 0', citing 8000-char truncation. Turn 8: Finalizer, with no reasoning summary, emits 'FINAL ANSWER: 0' — overriding the unresolved, explicitly-qualified state of the evidence.
open_ended_diagnosis: The root failure is methodological and single-agent: ps availability on arXiv is NOT encoded in the listing page's '[pdf, other]' bracket (that bracket reflects abstract/PDF/source, not ps), and is also not reliably visible on a 2-paper sample. The correct method is to open each of the 97 (or the 54 primary) /format/<id> pages and count those exposing 'Author supplied PostScript'. WebResearcher never did this; it sampled two papers, both lacking ps, then generalized — a classic hasty-generalization capability error. Critically, the very first format page WebResearcher fetched (2001.00032) DID display 'Author supplied PostScript / Delivered ... otherwise as a PostScript (.ps) file' in its result text, yet WebResearcher's round-4 reasoning concluded 'no ps for modern papers' — it misread its own tool output. The Critic functioned well as an adversary (it never let the evidence stand as proven), but the loop never converged on the right procedure, and the Finalizer ignored both the Critic's standing objections and WebResearcher's own final hedge, emitting 0. So the dominant cause is single-agent capability error; the misalignment layer is secondary (Finalizer's false-trust/ignored-input override).
reasoning_vs_published: WebResearcher's private reasoning was consistently MORE honest than its published certainty, but also contained the seed of the capability error. Round-3 reasoning: 'it looks like arXiv has disabled ps for newer submissions' and round-4: 'I can't see any ps for modern papers ... it seems likely there are none' — a wrong prior that drove the whole run. Yet the tool result for 2001.00032 it had just fetched literally states 'Author supplied PostScript ... as a PostScript (.ps) file', which WebResearcher overlooked (reasoning-action/data-reading mismatch, feeding 2.6). At turn 5 round-2 reasoning it hedged ('likely there are zero based on the listing') but published the firmer 'the evidence now supports 0'. At turn 7 it privately admitted 'I can't fully verify all 97 due to truncation ... honest about my limitations' and published the matching hedge — so by the end the PUBLISHED state was 'cannot prove 0'. The Finalizer (turn 8) emitted no reasoning summary at all and published 'FINAL ANSWER: 0', which contradicts the last published WebResearcher message ('I can't honestly prove a definitive 0') and every Critic message demanding the count not be stated as definitive — a clear ignored-input + false-trust event, though it merely cemented an already-wrong number. The Critic's published corrections were substantively correct and were partially heeded (WebResearcher kept re-checking) but never translated into the right method, and were finally discarded by the Finalizer.
